page: Amazon Web Services a1.4xlarge is an ARM-based instance powered by 16 dedicated physical cores of the first-generation AWS Graviton ARMv8 Cortex-A72 processor operating at 2.3 GHz. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture, the instance features 32 GB of system memory, providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. Hardware cache configuration includes 32 KB L1 data cache and 2 MB L2 cache, with no L3 cache present. The processor includes hardware AES encryption support but lacks x86-specific vector extensions. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 5 Gbps, and the configuration includes no local ephemeral storage or GPU accelerators.

Performance testing demonstrates stable multi-core capabilities, reflected in a stress-ng multi-core score of 23,858.27 and a single-core score of 1,491.48. In-memory caching performance for small 16 KB blocks reaches 566.18 GB/sec read bandwidth. Uncached large-block memory operations present hardware throughput limits, dropping to 32.43 GB/sec for 256 MB reads and 10.01 GB/sec for writes. Single-threaded benchmarks indicate modest execution speeds, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 409.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 5,725.18. Despite lower single-threaded metrics, the instance achieves balanced mid-range throughput in multi-core tasks, such as software compilation with Clang scoring 6,694.0 and database operations scoring 4,180.93.

The hardware configuration provides a budget-friendly ARM64 platform for scaled microservices, web infrastructure, and containerized services optimized for ARM architectures. Key benchmark strengths include high-throughput key-value store performance, recording 8.36 million Redis SET operations per second. Hardware tradeoffs include lower per-core execution speeds and limited uncached write bandwidth, making it less fitted for memory-intensive analytics. Best-suited applications include static web serving, Clang software compilation pipelines, lightweight containerized workloads, and Redis caching layers.
description: Amazon Web Services a1.4xlarge is an ARM-based instance powered by 16 dedicated physical cores of the first-generation AWS Graviton ARMv8 Cortex-A72 CPU running at 2.3 GHz on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance features 32 GB of system memory with 2.0 GB per core, a 5 Gbps network baseline, and hardware-accelerated AES encryption, while omitting local storage and GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations reveal steady multi-core performance, achieving a stress-ng multi-core score of 23,858.27 and 8.36 million Redis SET operations per second. However, large-block uncached memory writes (10.01 GB/sec) and single-core scores remain lower relative to modern x86 architectures. Featuring a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, a1.4xlarge provides a resource-dense ARM64 environment well suited for containerized microservices, web applications, Redis key-value caching, and parallel software compilation tasks.
